paths.description: Public homepage and search entry template; tested desktop, mobile, preferences, accessibility, performance, network, security, discoverability and memory.
Representative regional salon listing/search template and availability filters.
Representative salon detail and primary reservation CTA.
Primary booking journey entry through coupon/menu selection and visible four-step flow; stopped before making a real reservation.
Account/sign-in handoff to Recruit ID, including labels, autocomplete and invalid empty submission inspection.
Representative invalid route to assess recovery.

findings.summary: Dark preference is ignored
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical to the light capture; the probe reports colorScheme "normal", light foreground colours, and no prefers-color-scheme CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() for all surfaces.

findings.summary: Contrast preferences are unsupported
findings.evidence: The CSS preference probe found no forced-colors or prefers-contrast rules; Lighthouse also found two ordinary-state controls at only 3.42:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations and verify controls retain visible boundaries and text.

findings.summary: Route and state changes are abrupt
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection across the MPA templates found no view-transition-name or @view-transition usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for compatible navigations with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-state-aware chrome
findings.evidence: The homepage is 4,570 CSS px tall, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state container query, progress indicator, or responsive sticky-header treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries or a lightweight progress/condensed-header treatment on long result and detail pages.

findings.summary: A large modal obscures the primary content on arrival
findings.evidence: The desktop and mobile first-load screenshots show a gender-selection panel covering the search interface before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer the preference prompt until contextually useful, keep the page usable, and provide clear light-dismiss.

findings.summary: The blocking overlay is not a semantic dialog
findings.evidence: The overlay is visible in screenshots, but the DOM probe found no dialog or role=dialog element.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the modal with <dialog>, labelled semantics, focus management, Escape handling, and platform close behaviour.

findings.summary: Advertising and dense chrome crowd the content
findings.evidence: The first viewport devotes both side rails to animated campaign creative, adds a centered overlay, dense tab chrome, and a right account rail around a narrow content column.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer nonessential campaign chrome and prioritise the search and booking content.

findings.summary: Mobile receives a scaled desktop page
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 viewport the layout reports no viewport meta and a 1,311px layout viewport; the screenshot shows the entire desktop page shrunk to unreadable size.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a correct viewport meta tag and rebuild templates with intrinsic, fluid layouts that reflow at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Components do not respond to available container space
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container rules, and every representative mobile screenshot shows desktop components uniformly scaled rather than reorganised.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container queries to reused search cards, navigation, sidebars, and salon cards.

findings.summary: Most controls are smaller than touch guidance
findings.evidence: The objective probe measured 495 of 511 visible controls below 44px in at least one dimension; many links are 11-18px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase hit areas to at least 44x44 CSS px, preserve visible focus, and avoid hover-only interactions.

findings.summary: Measured mobile load performance is poor
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 35.5s, TBT 960ms, Speed Index 9.9s, and performance 0.37; the separate trace measured LCP 1.93s under a lighter run, showing condition sensitivity but not negating the throttled result.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, remove tag overhead, and establish CWV budgets with field monitoring.

findings.summary: JavaScript blocks the main thread under mobile conditions
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 960ms TBT; the trace also recorded two long tasks, while the page loads 94 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks and defer nonessential analytics and advertising scripts until consent or idle.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is burdened by parser-blocking resources and weak caching
findings.evidence: The HAR identified two VeryHigh parser stylesheets, several parser-inserted classic scripts, 353 requests, missing cache headers, and a 2.14s document request. DOM confirmation shows the core CSS in head.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer classic scripts, reduce critical CSS, add durable caching, and remove avoidable dependency chains.

findings.summary: The page ships large unused and duplicated script payloads
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1,327 KiB unused JavaScript; the HAR transfers 3.34MB of scripts and shows repeated tag destinations and duplicated vendor loads.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit tag-manager destinations, remove duplicate pixels, and conditionally load code only when needed.

findings.summary: Many image links lack a programmatic name
findings.evidence: The image primitive reports 71 images without alt and the DOM probe found 29 empty anchors without text, aria-label, or image alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful linked images concise alt text, mark decorative images empty-alt, and name every control.

findings.summary: Key app-install controls fail text contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found two controls at 3.42:1 (#fff on #d36985), below the required 4.5:1 for their text size.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the pink surface or change text colour and verify all states with automated and visual contrast tests.

findings.summary: Semantic structure is weak despite visible browser focus
findings.evidence: The probe found zero main/nav/header/footer/role landmarks and multiple empty headings; Lighthouse found a skipped heading level.
findings.suggestedFix: Add semantic landmarks, remove empty headings, and enforce a logical heading hierarchy while retaining the visible focus outline.

findings.summary: Text is unreadable at a common mobile viewport
findings.evidence: The 360px screenshots show desktop text compressed to only a few pixels because the page is scaled instead of reflowed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real mobile viewport, responsive type sizing, and comfortable line lengths.

findings.summary: The page does not reflow for mobile or zoom
findings.evidence: No viewport meta is present; at 360px Chrome creates a 1,311px layout viewport and scales it to 0.275, preventing usable reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 without disabling zoom, then test reflow at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom.

findings.summary: Third-party analytics generate console errors
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured four CORS/network console errors from Yahoo analytics during load.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or correct failing analytics calls and monitor production console errors.

findings.summary: Document and image asset hygiene is inconsistent
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s mobile document reported quirks-mode/no doctype, while the desktop probe found HTML doctype, indicating variant inconsistency; 42 images lack dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a consistent standards-mode doctype and reserve image space with width/height or aspect-ratio.

findings.summary: Deprecated and redundant integrations reduce platform hygiene
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded a deprecated Attribution Reporting API warning and failed third-party integrations; 28 javascript: links replace normal platform controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated integrations and replace javascript: anchors with buttons or real links.

findings.summary: Many controls are uncrawlable and the page lacks mobile viewport metadata
findings.evidence: The probe counted 28 javascript: links; Lighthouse listed 11 uncrawlable anchors, and no viewport meta exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions, real href URLs for navigation, and add a mobile viewport meta tag.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks share and organization metadata
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found no Open Graph, Twitter card, or JSON-LD on the homepage, although salon/detail templates do expose JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite structured data and Open Graph/Twitter metadata to index templates.

findings.summary: Transport hardening and cookie policy are unsafe
findings.evidence: The page is HTTPS, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent; 44 cookies were flagged insecure and HPB_SESSION_ID is SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, a strict CSP, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark every HTTPS cookie Secure and tighten SameSite.

findings.summary: Tracking is exceptionally broad on first load
findings.evidence: The tracker probe saw 55 third-party origins and eight known tracker domains; 337/353 HAR requests and 4.54MB/4.66MB transferred were classified third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate nonessential tracking on informed consent, consolidate vendors, minimise identifiers, and batch essential analytics.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no HSTS, clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy the missing defense headers and verify framing, referrer, permissions, and XSS protections.

findings.summary: Layout CSS is not writing-mode resilient
findings.evidence: The homepage correctly declares lang=ja, but the CSS probe found zero logical-property rules versus 25 physical left/right/width/height rules; the Recruit login redirect declares en-GB for Japanese copy.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical CSS properties and correct the login document language to Japanese.

findings.summary: Image delivery uses legacy, eager, nonresponsive assets
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 86 use legacy formats, none use modern formats, 59 below-fold images are not lazy, and 35 lack srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, responsive srcset/sizes, intrinsic dimensions, and lazy-load below-fold imagery.

findings.summary: Background marketing work dominates the load
findings.evidence: The page makes 353 requests, including 94 scripts and 70 fetches, with repeated analytics destinations and failed beacon traffic on first load.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate pixels and defer or batch nonessential background requests.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts consume nearly the entire transfer budget
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 4.54MB of 4.66MB transferred; Google Tag Manager alone contributes 2.31MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party byte/request budget and load vendors only after consent and demonstrated value.

findings.summary: The booking service exposes no structured agent capability
findings.evidence: The page is 93% visible without JS, but the capability probe found no WebMCP registration; agents must infer actions from hundreds of links and forms.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose narrowly scoped, confirmable search and booking tools through WebMCP/agentic forms.

findings.summary: The static homepage has a disproportionately large heap footprint
findings.evidence: The baseline heap contains 886,774 nodes and 49.9MB self size before meaningful interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce third-party runtimes and duplicated libraries, then set heap/node budgets for the homepage.
